text: In July of 2013 we said "the employer mandate" — forty-six of us at our peak on the seventeenth. We said "the student success act," forty-two of us, cresting on the nineteenth. On the seventeenth we converged again: thirty-seven on "the fairness for american families act," thirty-four on "mandate delay act," thirty-two on "the authority for mandate delay act." Todd Young said each of those three first, on the eleventh. Six days later twenty-eight of us said "2668 the fairness for american families"; Andy Barr said it first, that same day. Twenty-seven of us said "the individual mandate." Twenty-six of us said "and risk management." Much of that month our record narrows to one week, one Wednesday, and a small set of bills we named the same way at the same time. We report this as we found it.
